headline: Awarded red light camera contract to Sitestream LLC, adopted red light camera ordinance, and recommended Centre Square property sales to Carrier Construction.
summary: The council changed the traffic ordinance to cover only red light cameras, not speed cameras. It also recommended sales of two Centre Square North Main Street parcels and set a moratorium on new or expanded smoke and vape shops starting November 1, 2026. Residents spoke about red light cameras and storm drain flooding during public participation.
decisions: Confirmed Richard Webster to the Economic & Community Development Commission, term to 12/29, by voice vote.
Confirmed Paden Dickinson as regular member of the Historic District Commission, term to 1/30, by voice vote.
Confirmed Kiana Small as regular member of the Planning Commission, term to 7/28, by voice vote.
Confirmed Keith William Odume as alternate member of the Planning Commission, term to 7/30, by voice vote.
Confirmed Dianna Lynne Tack as regular citizen member of the Youth & Community Services Commission, term to 1/29, by voice vote.
Confirmed Ryan Martin as alternate member of the Zoning Commission, term to 12/28, by voice vote.
Recalled T. Hick from the Charter Revision Commission and appointed Jeffrey Scott Demarest, by voice vote.
Confirmed six members of the BEHS Roof Building Committee by voice vote.
Placed on file a New Hire Report for September 2026.
Approved $90,408.79 in tax refunds, unanimous vote.
Authorized the Bristol Police Department to apply for and accept three state-funded traffic safety grants, unanimous vote.
Authorized a parking license agreement at 182 North Main Street for Fire Department employees, unanimous vote.
Authorized a $32,749.09 lease with bibliotheca for library RFID equipment and software, unanimous vote.
Authorized agreements for a Phase I Assessment of 296 Riverside Avenue with a grant of up to $5,000 and a $500 City match, unanimous vote.
Referred the potential sale of Lot #6, Southeast Bristol Business Park, to the Planning Commission and Real Estate Committee, unanimous vote.
Accepted a $3,150,000 HUD award for Bristol ASHER/CPAT pre-construction and referred it to the Board of Finance, unanimous vote.
Authorized execution of an EPA Administrative Order on MS4 compliance, unanimous vote.
Approved a $30,500 amendment to Contract 2P25-044 for Andrews Street culvert engineering, raising the total to $222,800, unanimous vote.
Approved a $38,500 amendment to Contract 2P25-045 for Mellen Street culvert engineering, raising the total to $171,817.36, unanimous vote.
Approved Amendment No. 3 to Contract 2C26-002 for $95,824.97 at the Beals Community Center, unanimous vote.
Placed on file a positive referral for review of Perkins Street, Map 19, Lot 10, for the City to accept 7.5 acres of open space, unanimous vote.
Placed on file a positive referral for review of 510 Perkins Street, Map 60, Lot 16-3, unanimous vote.
Placed on file a positive referral for sale of city land at 21 Tuttle Road to 93 Tuttle Road owners, unanimous vote.
Placed on file a positive referral for sale of a small City right-of-way piece next to 99 Main Street, unanimous vote.
Placed on file a positive referral for sale of North Main Street, Map 30, Lot 3, unanimous vote.
Placed on file a positive referral for sale of North Main Street, Map 30, Lot 1, unanimous vote.
Approved a Page Park design contract amendment with Weston & Sampson, raising the total to $2,190,190.00, unanimous vote.
Awarded Contract 2P26-002 for the Update on 2018 Plan of Conservation and Development to IMEG Corp., $153,500, unanimous vote.
Accepted donation of 7.5 acres of open space at Parcel 19-10 Perkins Street, unanimous vote.
Authorized a quit claim of a strip of land to the owner of 99 Main Street, unanimous vote.
Approved use of 30 Cross Street as a joint training facility for Fire and Police, unanimous vote.
Accepted Accurate Mechanical LLC's $211,000 offer for 81 Church Avenue, unanimous vote.
Approved proceeding with sale of part of 21 Tuttle Road to 93 Tuttle Road for $1,500, unanimous vote.
Approved a resolution creating a Charter Revision Commission, 7-0 roll call.
Approved renewing the Beals Senior Community Center lease with Bristol-Burlington Health District, $10,154.77 per month, unanimous vote.
Adopted amendments to the traffic ordinance on red light cameras, 6-1 vote.
Awarded the Red Light Traffic Safety Camera Program contract to Sitestream LLC, 6-1 vote.
Approved a moratorium on new or expanded smoke and vape shops, effective November 1, 2026, through May 1, 2028, as a Zoning Commission motion placed on record.
Amended Edgewood Pre-K Academy construction contract, raising the guaranteed maximum price to $29,873,359, unanimous vote.
Adopted the Senior Volunteer Tax Relief Program resolution, 7-0 roll call.
Adopted the Vision Zero resolution with a goal of eliminating roadway deaths and serious injuries by 2046, 7-0 roll call.
Approved a six-month extension of the Pequabuck River Trail state grant, 7-0 roll call.
Approved a three-month extension of the Flood Resilience Plan state grant, 7-0 roll call.
Recommended sale of parcel 30-1 to Carrier Construction Inc. for $1 with an Enterprise Zone tax abatement schedule, unanimous vote.
Recommended sale of parcel 30-3 to Carrier Construction Inc. for $250,000 with an Enterprise Zone tax abatement schedule, unanimous vote.

decision_evidence.quote: Richard Webster – Appointment – term to 12/29. Replaced T. Hick. Confirming motion by Council Member Hahn. Motion passed in voice vote.
Paden Dickinson – Appointment as regular member – term to 1/30. Replaced J. St. John. Confirming motion by Council Member Rosengren. Motion passed in voice vote.
Kiana Small – Appointment as regular member – term to 7/28. Replaced J. Soares. Confirming motion by Council Member Rosengren. Motion passed in voice vote.
Keith William Odume – Appointment as alternate member – term to 7/30. Replaced K. Small. Confirming motion by Council Member Tyler. Motion passed in voice vote.
Dianna Lynne Tack – Appointment as regular member (Citizen Rep) – term to 1/29. Replaced C. Garay. Confirming motion by Council Member Seymour. Motion passed in voice vote.
Ryan Martin – Appointment as alternate member – term to 12/28. Replaced M. Patton. Confirming motion by Council Member Tyler. Motion passed in voice vote.

To recall the appointment of T. Hick who recently was appointed to the Board of Education and to appoint Jeffrey Scott Demarest to replace him. No term. Confirming motion by Council Member Rosengren. Motion passed in voice vote.
BEHS Roof Building Committee Michael Higgins – Appointment representing educational staff ... Confirming motion by Council Member Dickau. Motion passed in voice vote.
To place on file the New Hire Report for the month of September, 2026.
To approve the Tax Refunds as follows – ... Total $90,408.79

To authorize the Bristol Police Department to apply for and accept the following State-funded grants: Distracted Driving High Visibility Enforcement Grant, DUI Enforcement Grant, and Speed & Aggressive Driving Grant.

To authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute a parking license agreement with the owner of 182 North Main Street to allow Bristol Fire Department employees to use the parking lot for a period of approximately two weeks while renovations are completed in the Department's parking area.
To authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute a lease agreement with bibliotheca for the acquisition of RFID equipment and software in the amount of $32,749.09.

To authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to sign any and all agreements associated with an Assessment grant from the Naugatuck Valley Council of Governments (NVCOG) for up to $5,000, including a City match commitment of $500, to perform a Phase I Assessment of the city-owned parcel at 296 Riverside Avenue.

To refer the potential sale of Lot #6 of the Southeast Bristol Business Park to the Planning Commission for completion of a Connecticut General Statutes 8-24 Report, and to the City Council Real Estate Committee for completion of a Connecticut General Statutes 7-163e Public Hearing for the sale of municipally owned property.

To accept the award of $3,150,000 from HUD to begin pre-construction activities for the Bristol ASHER/CPAT facility, to authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute any and all documents related to this award, and to refer the matter to the Board of Finance for their action.
To authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute an EPA Administrative Order regarding MS4 compliance (CWA-AO-R01-FY26-22).

To authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute an amendment to Contract 2P25-044 with KS Engineers in the amount of $30,500 to provide structural engineering services for the Andrews Street culvert replacement, increasing the contract amount from $192,300 to $222,800.

To authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute an amendment to Contract 2P25-045 with WMC Engineers in the amount of $38,500 to provide structural engineering services for the Mellen Street culvert replacement, increasing the contract amount from $133,317.36 to $171,817.36.

To authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute Amendment No. 3 to Contract 2C26-002, Renovations at the Beals Community Center – Bristol-Burlington Health District Space, with Orlando Annulli & Sons, Inc., in the amount of $95,824.97, increasing the total contract amount from $2,244,004.00 to $2,339,828.97.

To place on file a positive referral for a C.G.S. Section 8-24 review of Perkins Street, Map 19, Lot 10 for the City of Bristol to accept ownership of the 7.5 acres of open space property currently owned by the Clinton Roberts Foundation.

To place on file a positive referral for a C.G.S. Section 8-24 review of 510 Perkins Street, Map 60, Lot 16-3 for the City of Bristol to obtain the property consisting of 3 acres owned by the Clinton Roberts Foundation, and not waive the right of first refusal.

To place on file a positive referral for a C.G.S. Section 8-24 review of 21 Tuttle Road, Map 07, Lot 30 and 93 Tuttle Road, Map 07, Lot 30C for the City of Bristol to sell approximately 5,367 sq. ft. of city-owned property at 21 Tuttle Road to the owners of 93 Tuttle Road, Map 07, Lot 30C.

To place on file a positive referral for a C.G.S. Section 8-24 review of 99 Main Street, Map 30, Lot 66 for the City of Bristol to sell a small piece of the City right-of-way immediately adjacent to 99 Main Street.
To place on file a positive referral for a C.G.S. Section 8-24 review for the sale of the property located at North Main Street, Map 30, Lot 3.
To place on file a positive referral for a C.G.S. Section 8-24 review for the sale of the property located at North Main Street, Map 30, Lot 1.
To amend Contract 2P22-010 Design of Renovations and Improvements at Page Park with Weston & Sampson Engineers, Inc. in the amount of $330,700 for a revised contract amount of $2,190,190.00
To award Contract 2P26-002 Update on 2018 Plan of Conservation and Development, to IMEG Corp. in the amount of $153,500.00
To accept the donation of vacant land known as Parcel 19-10 Perkins Street consisting of 7.5 acres of open space from the Clinton S. Roberts Foundation Inc.
To authorize the City of Bristol to Quit Claim a strip of land to the owner of property known as 99 Main Street, Map 30, Lot 66
To authorize the use of city-owned property known as 30 Cross Street, Assessor's Map 4, Lot 13-1, to be utilized as a joint regional training facility for the Fire and Police Departments.
To accept the offer from Accurate Mechanical LLC or its assigns, for the purchase of city-owned property known as 81 Church Avenue, Assessors Map 43, Lot 22, for the sale price of $211,000.
To proceed with the proposed sale of part of municipal property located at 21 Tuttle Road, Map 7, Lot 30 to 93 Tuttle Road, Map 7, Lot 30C.
To approve a resolution creating a Charter Revision Commission. ... RESOLUTION ADOPTED: YES – 7; NO – 0; ABSTAIN – 0.

it was unanimously voted: To authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to renew a lease agreement with Bristol-Burlington Health District for city-owned property located at 240 Stafford Avenue known as the Douglas A. Beals Senior Community Center
it was voted 6 - 1: To adopt amendments to Chapter 14 Motor Vehicles and Traffic, Article IV Moving Violations, Division 1, Sections 14-76 through 14-88 of the Bristol Code of Ordinances

it was voted 6 - 1: To award Contract 2P27-004 Red Light Traffic Safety Camera Program, to Sitestream LLC, and to authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute any and all documents necessary to effectuate said contract. (Council Member Tyler voted “No.”)

Motion to approve Application #AZR 26-03 with the following: ... 3. The Moratorium on the Establishment or Expansion of Smoke and Vape Shops, in all zones, shall become effective on November 1, 2026. The moratorium shall expire on May 1, 2028, unless repealed or superseded by an amendment to the Zoning Regulations.

On motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded by Council Member Dickau, it was unanimously voted: To amend Contract 2P26-051 Construction Management At Risk for the Renovation of Edgewood Pre-K Academy with D'Amato+Downes Joint Venture in the amount of $28,217,964.12 bringing their GMP to $29,873,359

To approve a resolution adopting a Senior Volunteer Tax Relief Program for senior citizens who volunteer their services to qualifying entities in the City. ... RESOLUTION ADOPTED: YES – 7; NO – 0; ABSTAIN – 0.

To approve a resolution implementing the Vision Zero Initiative in Support of Safe, Healthy and Equitable Mobility, establishing a goal of eliminating roadway fatalities and serious injuries on City of Bristol streets by 2046 ... RESOLUTION ADOPTED: YES – 7; NO – 0; ABSTAIN – 0.

To approve a resolution authorizing Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu to execute the necessary contract amendment on behalf of the City for a six-month extension of CTDEEP Grant (RTG Contract CNT 2023-259) ... RESOLUTION ADOPTED: YES – 7; NO – 0; ABSTAIN – 0.

To approve a resolution authorizing Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu to execute the necessary contract amendment on behalf of the City for a three-month extension of CTDEEP Grant (RTG Contract CNT 2025-020) ... RESOLUTION ADOPTED: YES – 7; NO – 0; ABSTAIN – 0.

To recommend Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu, or Acting Mayor, to execute a Purchase and Sale Agreement and to complete the property transaction, subject to the approval of Corporation Counsel, with Carrier Construction Inc. or its assigns for the sale and redevelopment of the Centre Square North Main Street property, identified as parcel 30-1 on the City land records, for the purchase price of $1 to construct a parking area and publicly accessible green space.

To recommend Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu, or Acting Mayor, to execute a Purchase and Sale Agreement and to complete the property transaction, subject to the approval of Corporation Counsel, with Carrier Construction Inc. or its assigns for the sale and redevelopment of the Centre Square North Main Street property, identified as parcel 30-3 on the City land records, for the purchase price of $250,000
